title: Window and Door Rebates in Kamloops 2026: $100 Each, Up to $2,000
desc: Kamloops homes can claim $100 per window or door from BC Hydro. Half of households live in pre-1981 homes and January lows average -6.1°C. Rules and steps.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Kamloops
lead: Kamloops has some of the oldest housing and the biggest temperature swings of any BC city we cover. Hot dry summers and cold winters both make old windows costly.
cards_heading: What BC Hydro pays for windows and doors in Kamloops
cards_intro: We re-read BC Hydro's window and door page on October 2, 2026. The rebate is for homes heated mainly by electricity. FortisBC lists $100 per opening for its gas customers, except in the City of Vancouver.

cards.title: Windows and doors
cards.note: Paid for each window or door that replaces an existing one between a heated space and outdoors.

cards.title: Cap
cards.note: That is 20 openings at $100 each. A bay window counts as one opening.

cards.title: Energy rating
cards.note: The window or door must have a maximum U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K, which is BC Hydro's Tier 2 level.

cards.title: More than one upgrade
cards.note: BC Hydro adds a bonus when you finish more than one eligible upgrade.

cards.title: Lower incomes
cards.note: Income-qualified customers can apply for free upgrades.

after_cards:
A Kamloops 1960s bungalow

A bungalow with 10 windows, a front door and a side door is 12 openings. That pays $1,200. Windows with a good U-factor also keep afternoon summer heat down, which helps if the house uses air conditioning.
sections: The 2021 Census counted 39,915 households in Kamloops. About 20,275 (51%) live in homes built before 1981, and 9,895 are owner-occupied detached houses from that period. Detached houses are 50% of households and 19% live in apartments.
A dry climate with real swings

Kamloops's average January low from 2015 to 2024 was -6.1°C and the coldest day was -34.3°C. Summers are hot and dry. Good windows work against both, which means they can pay off year-round if the house is cooled in summer.

The home must be mainly electric-heated, at least 12 months old and a primary residence. The BC Hydro account holder applies, or signs a consent form for someone else to apply. Condos and apartments are covered by a separate program. Outbuildings and garages are not eligible.
Each rough opening counts as one. A bay window is one. Skylights are excluded. Units need a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower and a listing from CSA, Intertek, Labtest, QAI or NFRC.

The rebate needs a U-factor of 1.22 W/m2-K or lower, and lower means less heat loss. Many window labels show the older imperial scale instead. To convert, multiply the imperial number by 5.678. A label that says U-0.30 equals 1.70 W/m2-K, which is too high. A label that says U-0.21 equals about 1.19 W/m2-K and passes. Ask the contractor to quote the metric value for each model so you do not have to convert.

BC Hydro pays a bonus of up to $2,000 when you finish more than one eligible upgrade, but its page does not give a formula, so ask when you apply. FortisBC lists a $300 second-upgrade bonus or an EnerGuide improvement bonus of $750 to $2,000. Windows pair naturally with insulation, since both cut heat loss through the building envelope.

BC Hydro sends income-qualified customers to the CleanBC Better Homes Energy Savings Program instead, and the two cannot be combined. The 2026 program document lists no insulation or window rebates, so the free Energy Conservation Assistance Program is the route to ask about.
claim_steps: Check the home is electric-heated and a primary residence.
Get quotes that list the U-factor of each unit.
Photograph each label on installation day.
Keep the invoice and apply within six months.
Add insulation to the same application to check the bonus.
faq: Do windows help in a Kamloops summer?
A lower U-factor slows heat flow in both directions, so they help against summer heat as well as winter cold.
The average January low was -6.1°C and the coldest day in 2015 to 2024 was -34.3°C.
What if I heat with gas?
FortisBC lists $100 per opening for gas customers.
